name: Rebellions Rebel100
memory_bandwidth_basis: Vendor-published: 144 GB HBM3E at 4.8 TB/s. Separately, the same page claims the predictive DMA engine 'enables 2.7 TB/s effective bandwidth' for KV data - that is a different quantity (the achievable rate for KV prefetch on long-context decode) and is deliberately not recorded as the memory bandwidth figure.
notes: Vendor is asic-other because 'rebellions' is not in the schema enum; the real vendor is Rebellions (South Korea). Explicitly labelled 'Compute (Dense)' by the vendor, so both rows are genuinely dense. THE HIERARCHY POINT: this is one of the few parts where the inter-chiplet link, not the memory, is the architectural story. A full-chip on-chip mesh over UCIe-Advanced runs at 1 TB/s per bidirectional channel at 11 ns latency, so the four chiplets present as one virtual die with no software-visible boundary - 11 ns is roughly a register-to-register hop, which is the mechanism behind the 'no stalls in sparse or imbalanced workloads' claim. Against 4.8 TB/s of HBM3E at 144 GB, that gives 213 FLOP/byte FP16 and 427 FP8, so batch-1 decode remains memory-bound but 144 GB of capacity is enough to hold a large model resident, which is the combination large-model inference actually wants. The predictive, software-controlled DMA prefetching KV data ahead of the MXU is a software-visible optimization, so it is a tuning surface rather than a fixed property. Process node and die size are not published. Shipping status: RebelServer and RebelRack are in production with paying operators (SK Telecom's A.X K1 sovereign LLM ran on RebelServer per July 2026), and the vendor claims native PyTorch 2.x / vLLM / Triton support. Dense/sparse is not separately stated for FP8, and the vendor's own perf/watt claims (3.8x vs a current-gen GPU node) are marketing.
